football_evidence.question: Can East Carolina stop Temple’s run game?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward East Carolina, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.0 of the 2.5 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When East Carolina has the ball (big plays through the air): East Carolina’s offense turns 10.1% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Temple’s defense gives up explosive gains on 15.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Temple has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Temple’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.2% of its dropbacks, and East Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Temple has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Temple’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 16.9% of its runs, and East Carolina’s defense stops 31.8% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
Jaxon Smolik has completed 16 of 27 passes (59.3%) for 129 yards, 4.8 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 1 interception in four games for Temple, and has been sacked on 4 of 31 dropbacks.
contradicting: When Temple has the ball (big plays through the air): Temple’s offense turns 15.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and East Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.1% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Temple has the ball (big plays on the ground): Temple’s offense turns 10.5% of its runs into explosive gains, and East Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When East Carolina has the ball (the red zone): East Carolina’s offense succeeds on 32.3% of its red-zone plays, and Temple’s defense allows success on 49.8% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).

When East Carolina has the ball (big plays on the ground): East Carolina’s offense turns 5.5% of its runs into explosive gains, and Temple’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

Mitch Griffis has completed 53 of 97 passes (54.6%) for 605 yards, 6.2 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for East Carolina, and has been sacked on 7 of 104 dropbacks.
